title: Token Cohort Compressor: dynamic microbatch shaping for padding reduction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Large variance in request sequence lengths causes high padding overhead and suboptimal kernel utilization in the serving runtime. This ticket implements a lightweight runtime component (Token Cohort Compressor) that groups in-flight requests into length-cohorts using a cheap fingerprint and continuously reshapes micro-batches to minimize padding while preserving latency SLOs. Goals: reduce average padded tokens per batch by >=25% on mixed workloads and improve GPU kernel occupancy for common kernel implementations without increasing tail latency.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration with prefill + decode scheduler producing cohort-based microbatches in production-like load tests
Padded-tokens-per-batch reduced by >=25% vs baseline on the mixed-traffic benchmark (see benchmark links)
Median tail latency (p50/p95) no worse than 5% relative to baseline for <512 token requests
Kernel selection logs include cohort-hint tags and match expected kernel affinity >= 90% of time
Feature gated rollout with metrics dashboard and emergency rollback path
benchmarks: baseline: mixed-traffic sim, avg padded tokens/batch = 8.4, p95 latency = 196ms
target: avg padded tokens/batch <= 6.3, p95 latency <= 206ms
implementation_notes: Fingerprinting: compute 8-bit length fingerprint from request token-count + hash(prompt-type) to avoid expensive histogram maintenance
Cohort windows: maintain N=16 light-weight cohorts per worker; assign incoming request to nearest cohort by fingerprint distance
Microbatch reshaping: when assembling a prefill microbatch, prefer filling cohorts first; allow up to 10% slot pooling across adjacent cohorts to prevent starvation
Kernel hints: attach cohort size & median-seqlen to request metadata so kernel selector can prefer pre-compiled kernels optimized for that shape
KV cache interaction: when cohorting prefill for decoder workloads, ensure KV cache locality by preferring requests with similar past model version and device affinity
Prefill priority: short requests get a small latency boost (priority buckets) to avoid tail growth; verify that overall padded savings are preserved
Fallbacks: if cohort occupancy low, fall back to runtime-wide packing to meet throughput SLO
Telemetry: emit cohort_id, cohort_median_len, padded_tokens_added, kernel_affinity, and microbatch_id for tracing & dashboards
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Cohorting could increase latency for long requests if prioritized incorrectly. Mitigation: short-request priority cap and canary targetting only non-critical shards first.
Risk: Kernel selector mismatches due to stale cohort hints. Mitigation: include time-to-live for cohort hints and verify at kernel selection time; add metrics to count hint mismatches.
Risk: Increased scheduler CPU overhead at high QPS. Mitigation: use sampled fingerprinting (1% expensive path) and simple integer ops on hot path; measure CPU in perf tests.
Risk: Interference with Dedicated autoscaling heuristics. Mitigation: run capacity-aware checks and respect autoscaler signals; disable cohorting under scale events.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests + benchmark runs in staging cluster (already done on branch)
2) Canary: enable cohorting on 5% of host pool for internal customers (1 week) with strict SLO guardrails
3) Expand to 25% after 1-week stability window and metric verification
4) Full rollout with runtime-1.21 if all acceptance criteria met
5) Immediate rollback flag available via console and infra feature-flag service
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: padded_tokens_per_batch increase > +10% vs baseline for 15m
SLOs: latency and availability must be tracked per-canary host pool
